title: Index Fundamentals
description: Understand how indexes accelerate queries and when they add overhead

data.text: Indexes are data structures that speed up data retrieval at the cost of additional storage and slower writes. Choosing the right index strategy is critical for query performance.

data.title: Key concepts
items: Leaf nodes store row pointers or full rows
Write amplification on INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

data.title: Create and use an index
data.content: Create an index on the email column for fast lookups.

data.title: Important
data.text: Indexes help reads but slow writes. Add indexes based on actual slow queries, not guesses.

items.question: How many indexes is too many?
items.answer: More than 5-6 per table is often excessive. Each index adds write overhead and storage.

items.question: Should I index every column in WHERE clauses?
items.answer: No. Consider selectivity, query frequency, and write volume before adding indexes.

items.question: Do indexes always speed up SELECT?
items.answer: No. Low-selectivity indexes or queries returning most rows may still scan the table.

data.title: Summary
points: Indexes trade write speed for read speed
Use B-tree indexes for equality and range queries
Monitor slow queries before adding indexes
data.takeaway: Indexes are most effective when targeted at selective, frequent queries on read-heavy tables.
